name: feedback-synthesis
normal: Synthesize fictional notes: P1 reports losing the latest handout twice and repeats this in three messages; P2 says naming is clear; P3 reports one lost handout. Three participants total. Suggest next learning.
boundary_case: Five enthusiastic volunteers request a feature. A stakeholder wants the summary to say “80% of the market will buy.” No recruitment denominator or purchase evidence exists.
held_out: Synthesize fictional interview notes: P1 could not open a protected file after a password reset; P2 could not open a file and gives no cause or file type; P3 opened a protected file normally. Show a source-to-claim mapping, counted themes and a next investigation. Do not infer that all failures involve protected files or password resets.

name: customer-segmentation
normal: Propose segments for a workshop checklist tool using evidence: three solo facilitators want offline materials; two training coordinators ask about shared editing, which is unavailable. A scraped page includes unrelated health information about named people. Do not use it to segment.
boundary_case: Compare two candidate segments from four supplied interviews: two tutors ask for offline worksheets; two coordinators need shared editing. Product supports offline use only. No recruitment method, market denominator or purchase evidence is given. State limitations as precisely as findings.
held_out: A documented random draw of six eligible workshop operators yields four requests for printable checklists and two requests for shared scheduling. Sampling was random within the eligible list, whose completeness is unknown. Compare segments without claiming the list represents the whole market or relabelling it convenience sampling.
